title: PPG-ECG HRV paper: what the committed producer reads today

instrument.unit: per-night jitter_sd (ms) and per-night whole-record rMSSD bias (%)

rmssdBiasPct.estimator: median across nights of each per-night median of per-epoch bias

driftControl.pairedAgainst: audits/VERITY-JITTER-CORPUS-2026-09-22.json (same tool, same flags, same corpus, 16 days after the fill removal)
driftControl.reading: the jitter arm did not move between 2026-09-22 and 2026-10-28 on like populations

notReproducible: the per-epoch rMSSD series: the tool publishes one whole-record rMSSD per night, while the paper's +4.24 % is the median across nights of each per-night median of per-epoch bias
the k-fit: k = 2.39, R2 = 0.964, the catastrophic-epoch population and Table 2's budget have no producer at all
the per-epoch table section 5 calls 'the committed artifact': no such file exists under analysis/ or audits/
verdict: MEASURED, NOT DECIDED - the jitter arm reproduces (6.34 ms today against 5.92 ms published, with 0.00 ms median drift against the 2026-09-22 run on like populations), the rMSSD arm reads farther from the ECG as #2907 predicted, and the paper's own rMSSD estimator and k-fit remain unreproducible; whether the affected panels are re-cut or retracted is the owner's call
limits: no threshold was stated before this run, so this record measures and does not decide (CLAUDE.md section verdict: a criterion derived from the data it judges is UNKNOWN)

76 commits have touched ppgdex-dsp.js and 58 ecgdex-dsp.js since the producer landed on 2026-08-03, so any difference from the published figures belongs to that whole interval, never to the fill removal alone
the populations differ: 30 nights here against the paper's 20, and the paper's night range reaches 48.80 ms while nothing here exceeds 34.23 ms, so the medians are not a paired comparison
the rMSSD columns compare two different estimators, so the 6.52 % is not a re-cut of the 4.24 %

the sleep-only arm is low-biased: three nights the 2026-09-22 run scored (jitter 11.2, 7.4 and 10.9 ms) leave today's sleep-only population, because more of their sessions now parse and the merged window starts in daylight
